title: The sultan's demand
hook: Namdev sings of a sultan who demanded a miracle, and of the Lord who saved him (Bhairao, Namdev)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gobind: the one thread through the beads and the water in every wave. Your line was everything is gobind.

Prove it. Two words that can corner anyone. Show me your God does something, right here, right now, or else. In one of his hymns, Namdev tells of the day a ruler said exactly that to him. Not a friend teasing, but a sultan, with power behind the words and Namdev's life on the table. The printer who sang that everything is Gobind is suddenly asked to make Gobind perform.
screen: `PROVE IT.` → `A SULTAN, AND A THREAT.` → `MAKE GOBIND PERFORM.`

segments.voice: The hymn is in Raag Bhairao, around Ang 1165. In paraphrase: the sultan says, listen, Namdev, let me see the works of your Lord. He has Namdev bound, and a dead cow is set before him. Bring this cow back to life, says the sultan, or I'll cut off your head right here. Now Namdev's answer, the heart of the day. How can this be? Nothing happens by my doing. Whatever the Lord does, that is what happens. He won't put on a show, or claim a power that isn't his. And he won't drop the Lord to save his neck either. The hymn holds him right there, under threat, honest about what he can and can't do. Then the turn. The hymn says the Lord came to Namdev's side, the cow rose up, and the sultan, shaken, came asking forgiveness. It tells the rescue quickly. It lingers longer on the moment before, when Namdev had nothing to offer but the truth. And look where the hymn puts the credit. Not on Namdev. He refused to be the miracle worker the sultan wanted. He stayed a devotee, and the saving came from beyond him. That's why today's line has two halves. Namdev was saved. He was never shown off.
screen: `LET ME SEE YOUR LORD'S WORKS.` · `NOTHING HAPPENS BY MY DOING.` · `UNDER THREAT, HE STAYS TRUE.` · `THE CREDIT GOES BEYOND HIM.` · then, large: `SAVED, NOT SHOWN.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one place in your life where someone wants you to perform: prove you're right, prove you're good enough, say what they want to hear. Notice where that pressure sits in your body, breathe out slowly, and let one honest sentence form: this is what I can do, and this is what I can't. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you breathe out.
Sultan. The ruler who ordered Namdev to raise a dead cow or die, and heard him say: nothing happens by my doing.
Your line: saved, not shown. Namdev stayed honest, and the credit went beyond him. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Namdev's hymn of the sultan is sung as gurbani, and Sikhs often recall it alongside the Gurus' teaching that devotees should not seek to display miraculous powers.

chat.says: When the sultan said prove it, why didn't Namdev just perform a miracle?
options: He said nothing happens by his doing; he stayed honest, and the credit went beyond him.
He tried, but his powers had faded with age, so the Lord had to step in instead.
He did: Namdev raised the cow himself to prove his own power to the sultan.
chat.meaning: In Bhairao Namdev answers: nothing happens by my doing; whatever the Lord does happens. He was saved, never shown off.

notes: Hymn 'sultaan poochhai sun be naamaa; dekhau raam tumhaare kaamaa... bismil gaoo dehu jeevaai; naatar gardan maarau thaai... baadisaah aisee kiu hoi; bismil keeaa na jeevai koi; meraa keeaa kachhoo na hoi; kar hai raam hoi hai soi' placed around Ang 1165–1166: confirm Ang range and the paraphrase.

The hymn's further details (the elephant, Namdev's mother, the Lord on Garuda, the offer of gold) are omitted; the rescue is summarized as 'the Lord came to Namdev's side, the cow rose, the sultan asked forgiveness'. Confirm the summary.
The sultan is named only as a ruler; the script avoids framing the episode as between religions. Confirm this framing is fair.
howItsDone: the Gurus' teaching against displaying miraculous powers is stated generally; confirm phrasing.
Original ਸੁਲਤਾਨੁ: confirm spelling as it appears in the hymn.
